questions.question: What does a linked braking system do?

options.text: It connects the front and rear brakes. When you use either brake lever, both brakes apply.
It connects the front brake to the gear shifter. The brake applies when you downshift.
It connects the rear brake to a foot control.
It connects the rear brake to a switch on the handlebar.

questions.correctAnswerText: It connects the front and rear brakes. When you use either brake lever, both brakes apply.
questions.explanation: A linked braking system connects the front and rear brakes on a motorcycle. When you use either brake lever, both brakes apply at the same time. Check your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: How can you discourage other vehicles from lane sharing?

options.text: Ride in the left portion of the lane.
Ride in the center portion of the lane.
Give dirty looks if another driver moves into your lane.
Ride in a zigzag pattern to fill up the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane to discourage other drivers from trying to squeeze into your space.

questions.question: When you see all of these at the same time, whose directions must you follow?
questions.correctAnswerText: A police officer.
questions.explanation: Always follow a police officer's directions. They override traffic signs and signals.

questions.question: When a group of motorcyclists rides through a curve, what formation should they use?
questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file formation.
questions.explanation: Use single-file formation when going through curves, turns, or entering/leaving highways. Staggered formation is used at other times.

questions.question: Which surface provides good traction?
questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Dry pavement provides good traction. Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, and painted lane markings all provide poor traction for motorcycles.

questions.question: In a normal turn, how should the motorcycle and rider move?

options.text: The motorcycle and rider should lean together.
The motorcycle and rider should lean in opposite directions.
The motorcycle should lean, but the rider should not.
The rider should lean, but the motorcycle should not.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle and rider should lean together.
questions.explanation: In normal turns, the motorcycle and rider lean together at the same angle. In slow, tight turns, only the motorcycle leans while the rider stays upright.

questions.question: When riding through curves, turns, or entering a highway, what is the best group formation?
questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file.
questions.explanation: Use single-file formation through curves, turns, and when entering or leaving highways. Staggered formation works best at other times.

questions.question: When riding downhill or shifting into first gear, what may you need to do?

options.text: Use your brakes to slow down before downshifting safely.
Flash your brakes to warn drivers behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your brakes to slow down before downshifting safely.
questions.explanation: Slow down with your brakes before downshifting. Downshifting at high speed can cause the motorcycle to lurch and the rear wheel to skid.

questions.question: If your throttle gets stuck, what should you do?

options.text: Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
Do not try to twist the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
questions.explanation: Try twisting the throttle back and forth to free it. If that does not work, use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch at the same time.

questions.question: Where should you place a load on your motorcycle?

options.text: Only on one side of the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible.
questions.explanation: Place loads as low as possible. High loads, such as on a sissy bar, raise the center of gravity and hurt balance. Distribute loads evenly on both sides of the motorcycle.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, you should:

options.text: Speed up to stop the wobble.
Hold the handlebars tight and slowly reduce speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars tight and slowly reduce speed.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up when your motorcycle wobbles. This makes it more unstable. Instead, hold the handlebars firmly and slowly reduce speed. Move your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you can. Do not use the brakes, as this can make the wobble worse.

questions.question: When you approach a four-way traffic light that is not working, you should:

options.text: Treat it like a stop sign.
Look both ways and go without stopping.
Look both ways and stop only if another vehicle is close.
Drive through because the light for other traffic may be working.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: If a four-way traffic light is not working, treat it like a stop sign. If a police officer is directing traffic, follow their directions.

questions.question: To help other drivers see you, you should wear:
questions.correctAnswerText: Bright-colored clothes.
questions.explanation: Wear bright-colored clothes so other drivers can see you better. Choose clothes that are easy to see both during the day and at night.

questions.question: ______ help direct riders into the correct lanes for turning.

options.text: White arrows painted on the road

questions.correctAnswerText: White arrows painted on the road
questions.explanation: White arrows painted on the road at intersections show you which direction to go from that lane. Follow any signs or signals with these arrows.

questions.question: If you need to brake while in a curve, you should:

options.text: Brake more gently than you would on a straight road.
Brake just as hard as you would on a straight road.
Wait until you leave the curve before braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake more gently than you would on a straight road.
questions.explanation: Tires have less grip when a motorcycle is leaning. Try to straighten your motorcycle before braking. If you must brake while turning, apply the brakes smoothly and gently.

questions.question: A motorcycle that fits you properly:

options.text: Lets you touch the ground with your feet while sitting down.
Has a seat at your waist level.
Has a seat 10 inches above your waist.
Has a seat 10 inches below your waist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets you touch the ground with your feet while sitting down.
questions.explanation: A properly-fitted motorcycle lets you touch the ground with your feet while you sit on the seat. Keep your feet on the footrests when riding.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, which part of your lane should you ride in?
questions.correctAnswerText: The center
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. This is safest. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle increases the risk of a crash. Riding on the far side may make the driver move back into your lane too soon.

questions.question: Small vehicles can look ______ and seem to be moving ______ than they really are.
questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away, slower
questions.explanation: Small vehicles like motorcycles can look farther away and seem to move more slowly than they actually do. This can make it hard for other drivers to judge where the vehicle is and how fast it is going.

questions.question: The best way to handle a driver who is tailgating you is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make rude gestures.
Speed up to create distance between you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: If you can, change lanes and let the tailgater pass. Do not speed up. The driver may tailgate you at higher speeds, making it more dangerous.

questions.question: If your front tire goes flat while riding:

options.text: The ride will feel too smooth.

questions.correctAnswerText: The steering will feel heavy.
questions.explanation: If your front tire goes flat, the steering will feel heavy. If your steering feels heavy, leave the road right away and check your tires.
